local.h: UN honors CNN founder Ted Turner
local.b: The United Nations held a celebration of life for Ted Turner, who died in May at 87. His daughter Laura Turner Seydel recalled his record $1 billion gift to UN causes in 1997 and urged guests to back the institutions that hold the world together.
local.title: UN honors late media mogul and CNN founder Ted Turner

goodnews.b: The 29-foot bronze by Atlanta artist Stan Mullins stands in Midtown's Pardis Park after a five-year effort led by Rostam Zafari of the nonprofit Nimruz.

local.h: Judge denies Lindsay Clancy's double jeopardy motion
local.b: Judge William Sullivan rejected the defense argument that a retrial after September's mistrial in the deaths of her three children would violate her rights.

goodnews.h: 51-year-old Chicago truck driver makes pro sumo debut
goodnews.b: Rupert Cintron got his shot when a new sumo league came through Chicago. "It's like life never ends if you don't let the dream end," he said.

local.h: Salvation Army to lose control of one of Denver's largest shelters
local.b: The change is part of a broader shake-up of the city's homeless services.
local.title: The Salvation Army will lose control of one of Denver’s largest shelters

local.h: City Park bandstand to be torn down after fire
local.b: Denver will build a nearly identical replacement in time for the 2027 City Park Jazz season.
local.title: The City Park bandstand is coming down after the fire

local.h: Denver and Littleton sue Bow Mar over gates on South Sheridan
local.b: The two cities are taking the small town to court over its plan to gate South Sheridan Boulevard.
local.title: The battle over Bow Mar’s gates is going to court

local.h: Claims center opens for Garden Grove evacuees
local.b: GKN Aerospace opened a center in Los Alamitos Tuesday to help residents evacuated during the Garden Grove chemical tank scare file for reimbursement from its $100 million claims program. Help is offered in English, Vietnamese, Spanish and Korean.
local.title: The company behind Garden Grove hazmat scare opens a center to help victims file claims

local.h: LAHSA shuts down computers over potential security issue
local.b: The homeless services agency told employees Friday to stay off its systems, and the order was still in place Monday. Its interim CEO said it was not yet clear whether personal information was accessed.
local.title: LAHSA shuts down its computers over ‘potential security issue’

local.h: California voters reject billionaire tax
local.b: Prop. 40 would have charged billionaires a one-time 5% tax on most of their wealth to fund healthcare. Opponents argued it would drive the wealthy out of the state.

local.h: Raman's mayoral win lifts hopes for transit and safer streets
local.b: Advocates are optimistic after Mayor-elect Nithya Raman, backed by bike lane supporters, defeated Mayor Karen Bass, who conceded Thursday.
local.title: Raman’s win triggers surge of optimism among advocates of transit and safer streets in LA

local.h: Man indicted in killing of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez
local.b: Brooklyn prosecutors indicted a city Department of Education worker in the Oct. 30 stabbing of Katie Suarez on a Bath Beach path. Police say surveillance shows him fleeing the scene.
local.title: Man indicted in stabbing murder of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez

local.h: Judge orders city to answer ICE shelter subpoena
local.b: A federal judge ruled City Hall must give ICE the names and birthdates of South Bronx migrant shelter residents with serious criminal histories. The Mamdani administration says it is evaluating next steps.
local.title: ICE subpoena puts a spotlight on the last emergency migrant shelter in NYC

local.h: Canal Street face-lift pushed into 2027
local.b: The city's Department of Transportation told a community board that concrete work on west Canal Street, planned for this fall, will slip to next year in the Reimagining Canal Street project.
local.title: Manhattan's Canal Street is getting a face-lift, but it'll take a while

local.h: East Harlem buildings head to auction despite City Hall push
local.b: Thirty-eight deteriorating buildings with about 850 mostly rent-stabilized apartments, formerly owned by bankrupt Emerald Equities Group, go to auction starting Tuesday. Mayor Mamdani's administration had backed a bid by affordable housing developer Spatial Equity to buy the portfolio first.
local.title: Rent-stabilized buildings hit auction block, despite Mamdani’s efforts to intervene

local.h: T-Mobile throttled affordable internet for low-income New Yorkers, AG says
local.b: T-Mobile agreed to improve service after the attorney general's office found it capped speeds and made the discounted plans hard to find. Only 15 households had enrolled.
local.title: T-Mobile slowed Internet to a crawl for NY low-income users, AG says

local.h: NJ Gov. Sherrill picks Shirley Emehelu as lieutenant governor
local.b: The former prosecutor and acting secretary of state replaces Dale Caldwell, who resigned in September. Women now hold New Jersey's two highest executive offices for the first time.
local.title: NJ Gov. Sherrill announces her new lieutenant governor pick

local.h: One dead in Hamilton Heights apartment fire
local.b: The fire started in a cluttered third-floor unit of a Riverside Drive building around 1:30 a.m. Five others, including two firefighters, were hurt. FDNY says 87 people have died in fires this year, up from 45 at this point last year.
local.title: 1 dead after early morning fire rips through Hamilton Heights apartment building, FDNY says

local.h: NYC expands Code Blue cold-weather help for homeless New Yorkers
local.b: The city is adding $25 million, 300 more outreach workers and 800 more beds for nights below freezing. More than two dozen people died in the cold last winter.
local.title: Mamdani says more help is coming to homeless New Yorkers living outside this winter

local.h: BHV Marais abruptly shuts its doors
local.b: The Paris department store closed Monday evening after an insurance policy lapsed during its bankruptcy process. Management says a new contract takes effect Tuesday, but unions fear it won't reopen.
local.title: Paris department store BHV forced to close doors

local.h: Ritz searched in Al-Fayed trafficking probe
local.b: Investigators searched the Ritz and other Paris landmarks tied to the late Mohamed Al-Fayed in a probe into accomplices in alleged human trafficking. People were held for questioning and his former Saint-Tropez estate was also investigated.
local.title: Ritz among Paris landmarks searched in Al-Fayed trafficking probe

local.h: France summons Iran's envoy over fridge sabotage
local.b: Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot summoned Iran's ambassador to protest the cyberattack on supermarket fridges, calling it the first large-scale sabotage attack on French territory. He said France will push for EU sanctions and rules nothing out.

local.h: France vows tough response to Iran-blamed supermarket cyberattack
local.b: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador will be summoned and EU sanctions sought over the October attack on hundreds of supermarket fridges.

local.h: Judo champion Teddy Riner runs for French president
local.b: The Olympic star announced a 2027 bid, citing concern about the rise of the far right as Marine Le Pen leads the polls.

local.h: Teachers and students call strikes and protests for Tuesday
local.b: Education unions and student groups plan a nationwide mobilization on Nov. 10 with a major march in Paris, citing staffing and funding concerns.

local.h: Murray questions ICE's $1.5 billion Tacoma detention deal
local.b: Sen. Patty Murray, set to chair Senate Appropriations, is pressing DHS about ICE's $1.5 billion contract to keep a private firm running the Northwest ICE Processing Center and whether ICE still plans to buy a new Seattle-area facility.
local.title: Washington state senator begins probe into deportation system after GOP loses congress

local.h: Washington Democrats win a supermajority in the state House
local.b: Democrats flipped at least seven seats and are on track for at least 66, their first two-thirds House majority since 1949.

local.h: Seattle School Board votes to authorize suit over trans sports ban
local.b: Directors voted unanimously Monday to let Superintendent Ben Shuldiner take legal action against Initiative 638, which bans transgender girls from girls' school sports.

goodnews.h: Granddaughter turns to social media to save 50-year-old La Palma
goodnews.b: Loren Jewett has given herself 30 days of videos to bring customers back to the Mexican restaurant her grandparents have run since 1976.

goodnews.h: Jimi Hendrix will be on Washington's $1 coin
goodnews.b: Gov. Bob Ferguson's office chose the Seattle guitar legend for the state's innovation coin, due in 2029.
